scenarios.title: Provide enough dynamic addresses without rewriting a held lease
scenarios.summary: Diagnose a partially successful client test and repair a dynamic range while retaining a held binding.
scenarios.objective: Keep one dynamic range entirely within 10.50.0.100–10.50.0.110 on 10.50.0.0/24; serve no additional subnet. Both new clients need distinct usable leases in both supplied cases, including the case with .100 and .101 occupied. Supply router 10.50.0.1, DNS 203.0.113.53 and a 600-second grant to each new client. Keep the supplied management lease, including its current options and timing, unchanged.
steps: Edit the supplied virtual configuration, run both client cases, inspect specific failures and retry.
scenarios.explanation: Choose a range inside the supplied allowed window with at least two free addresses in each test case. The reference uses .100 through .103: four addresses minus the two supplied occupied addresses leaves two. Supported alternatives such as .102 through .104 can also work. Keep router, DNS and duration correct; the existing held management binding is preserved rather than reacquired.
hints: Compare the number of free addresses with the two new clients in the busy case; occupied addresses are not available.
The endpoints are inclusive. A range with three addresses can leave only one when two are occupied. Any supported range within the allowed window with enough free addresses may work.
scenarios.simplifications: Offline legacy ISC-style configuration subset and deterministic logical clients, not an ISC daemon or packet capture. At most eight /1–30 subnets, one inclusive range of up to 256 addresses per subnet, numeric router/DNS options and bounded default/max lease durations. /31 and /32 are excluded special cases. Global parameters precede subnet declarations; local parameters precede range. Includes, hooks, static host declarations, router lists, shared networks, IPv6, failover and unmodeled syntax refuse honestly. No host files, commands, services, real network or wall clock. Renew is limited to an eligible held address during the supplied renewal window; no ISC NAK/cache/lease-file fidelity. ISC DHCP is EOL; this teaches an exam-listed legacy format, not a deployment recommendation.

initial.instructions: Keep one dynamic range entirely within 10.50.0.100–10.50.0.110 on 10.50.0.0/24; serve no additional subnet. Both new clients need distinct usable leases in both supplied cases, including the case with .100 and .101 occupied. Supply router 10.50.0.1, DNS 203.0.113.53 and a 600-second grant to each new client. Keep the supplied management lease, including its current options and timing, unchanged.

example.instructions: In the separate workshop, provide two new clients with distinct addresses from 10.60.0.100–10.60.0.110, router 10.60.0.1, DNS 203.0.113.53 and 600-second grants. Preserve the held management lease. Compare the available-address case with the case where .100 and .101 are already occupied.

scenarios.title: Repair inherited DHCP options and verify a renewing client
scenarios.summary: Diagnose option inheritance across two networks and distinguish new, renewing and untouched client settings.
scenarios.objective: Alpha clients need router 10.51.0.1 and DNS 203.0.113.53; beta clients need router 10.51.1.1 and DNS 203.0.113.54. Every new or renewed client needs a 600-second grant; evaluate both supplied occupancy cases. Keep alpha’s dynamic range inside .10–.20 and beta’s inside .50–.60 in their respective supplied /24 networks. Serve no other dynamic subnet. The management client renews at 300 virtual seconds and must receive the corrected alpha settings. Keep the untouched beta client’s supplied address, options and lease timing exactly unchanged.
steps: Edit the supplied virtual configuration, run both client cases, inspect specific failures and retry.
scenarios.explanation: Use global DNS .53 and a local beta DNS .54 override, with local .1 routers and an effective default duration of 600 seconds. Equivalent explicit per-subnet settings are supported. Keep dynamic ranges eligible for the supplied renewals and large enough in both occupancy cases. The management renewal receives new options; no action should rewrite the untouched held beta binding.
hints: A global DNS parameter supplies a default. A local option inside one subnet changes only that subnet’s inherited DNS.
Compare new and renewing clients with the untouched held client. Loading configuration is not a broadcast of new options to all current clients.

Tests advance virtual time by 300 seconds, renew management, then request leases for three new clients. The untouched beta client must keep its held binding.
